definition: A caricature is a portrayal that exaggerates its subject's most distinctive features, usually to amuse or to mock.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word caricature. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know caricature should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The courtroom artist kept her official sketches sober, but her notebook margins filled with caricatures — the judge all eyebrows, the prosecutor one enormous pointing finger.

An impression is gentler than a caricature: a comic's impression borrows a voice and a favorite phrase, while a caricature seizes the subject's most distinctive features and stretches them past life size.

Mockery goes further than caricature: a caricature bends its subject's features and keeps the likeness legible, while making a mockery of something abandons fidelity altogether — the original survives only as a target.

A lampoon is a written or staged attack that ridicules its target, and it can work by any weapon — mock praise, parody, or plain scorn. A caricature has one signature move: it seizes the subject's own most distinctive features and stretches them until they turn comic.

A cartoon is the drawn form — most newspaper caricatures are cartoons. But a caricature can live in prose or in a comedian's act, and plenty of cartoons exaggerate no one; the two words overlap without matching.

Caricature is the exact word because the drawing works by overloading real features: the cheeks, the trumpet, the obsession with tempo are all genuinely his, stretched until they turn comic.
A faithful likeness would have kept the proportions; the caricature keeps the man and inflates the evidence.
A caricature needs a real subject: the humor comes from recognizing actual features pushed too far, whether in a drawing, a prose sketch, or an act.

Her drawings were never cruel, but they were never neutral either: each teacher arrived as a caricature, one true feature hunted down and enlarged until it did all the talking.
